comments.text: Prediction in financial markets is an illusion; execution and risk management are the only reality. The market moves strictly on order-book liquidity and institutional delta/gamma hedging, not on horizontal trend lines or next-day opinions. Defining "above X is bullish, below Y is bearish" is just an unfalsifiable hedge—it guarantees being "right" regardless of what happens. Real trading isn't guessing tomorrow's direction; it's having a positive statistical expectancy, sizing defensively, and cutting losses without hesitation when invalidation hits.
